title: Cash and bank accounting (example)

role.summary: Looks after cash and bank accounts, the month-end bank reconciliation, petty cash and VAT data.
role.context: Works alone on this; the chief accountant reviews everything at month end.

stakeholders.name: Chief accountant
stakeholders.relationship: Reviews and approves the reconciliation every month

stakeholders.name: Finance team
stakeholders.relationship: Sends transfers and cheques to be recorded

tasks.name: Month-end bank reconciliation
tasks.why_priority: Only this person does it, and it must be done before the month closes

tasks.name: Count petty cash and close the safe
tasks.why_priority: Every day; a shortage must be known the same day

tasks.name: Approve a supplier payment
tasks.why_priority: Money leaves the company and is hard to get back

deadlines.what: Send the November reconciliation to the chief accountant
Send November VAT data to the external accountants

in_progress.next_step: Ask the finance team about cheque #4471

watch.why: The bank announced new fees from December

processes.name: Month-end bank reconciliation
processes.summary: Match the bank balance to the accounting system before the month is closed.
processes.trigger: First business day of the month, once the bank issues the statement

people.involvement: Reviews and approves the reconciliation file

steps.title: Download last month's statement
steps.detail: In online banking, choose the current account, set the period to last month and download it as PDF.
steps.why: The bank's figure is the most reliable starting point.
steps.check: The file name and date range match the month being closed.

pins.label: Set the period to last month

steps.title: Run the cash report in the accounting system
steps.detail: Set the date range from the 1st to the last day of the month and run the report.
steps.why: If the dates differ from the statement, the totals will not match.
steps.check: The opening balance equals last month's closing balance.

pins.label: 1st to last day of the month

steps.title: Compare the closing balances
steps.detail: Compare the closing balance on the statement with the one in the report.
steps.why: If they match the job is quick; if not, the difference must be found before closing.
steps.check: Write both balances in the reconciliation file.

steps.title: Find what is missing
steps.detail: Check cheques not yet presented first, then bank fees, then transfers that crossed the month end.
steps.why: The most common cause is a cheque the payee has not banked yet.
steps.branch_question: Did you find what is missing?

steps.title: Report a difference you cannot find
steps.detail: Record the difference in the reconciliation file with what you already checked, and tell the chief accountant.
steps.why: The chief accountant decides whether to close the month or wait.

steps.title: Record the result and send it
steps.detail: Fill in this month's reconciliation file and email it to the chief accountant by the 3rd.
steps.why: The chief accountant uses this file to close the books.
steps.check: The chief accountant replies to confirm.

rules.text: A difference of $5 or less can be booked as a bank fee without searching for it.
rules.why: Not worth the time, and it is almost always a fee.
rules.source: Summarised from the interview; not confirmed yet

rules.text: The bank statement is always the reference. Never change the bank figure to match the system.
rules.why: The bank figure is the real money.

troubleshooting.symptom: Opening balance differs from last month's closing balance
troubleshooting.cause: Someone edited a past entry in the system
troubleshooting.fix: Check the edit history in the system and tell the chief accountant.

scenarios.situation: At month end the balances differ by $500.
scenarios.question: What do you check first?
options: Cheques not yet presented
Call the bank straight away
Change the system figure to match
scenarios.explanation: Unpresented cheques are the most common cause, and you never change figures to make them match (R-002).

scenarios.situation: The difference is $3 and it looks like a transfer fee.
scenarios.question: Can you book it as a fee?
options: Yes, it is under $5
Yes, but the $5 limit is not confirmed yet, so note it in the file
No, always call the bank
scenarios.explanation: The $5 limit (R-001) is the AI's summary of the interview and still needs confirmation (OQ-001), so the chief accountant must see it.

processes.name: Prepare the monthly VAT data
processes.summary: Collect the month's purchase and sales VAT invoices and send them to the external accountants.
processes.trigger: Start of the month, after last month's sales are closed

people.involvement: Looks over the summary before it is sent

steps.title: Collect purchase VAT invoices
steps.detail: Gather the invoices from the paper file and from email.
steps.why: Purchase VAT without an invoice cannot be claimed.
steps.check: The number of invoices equals the purchases in the system.

steps.title: Run the sales VAT report
steps.detail: Reports › Sales VAT, choose last month and export to Excel.
steps.why: The external accountants use this file as it is.

steps.title: Check tax IDs and dates on the invoices
steps.detail: Check the company name, tax ID and date against the entry in the system.
steps.why: An invoice with wrong details cannot be used; the supplier must issue a new one.
steps.check: Wrong invoices are in the "to fix" folder with a list of suppliers to contact.

steps.title: Summarise for the chief accountant
steps.detail: Fill in purchase and sales VAT in the month's summary file and send it to the chief accountant.
steps.why: The chief accountant spots unusual totals faster.

steps.title: Send to the external accountants
steps.detail: Send the sales report, the summary and scans of the purchase invoices by the 10th of the following month.
steps.why: They need time to file before the deadline.
steps.check: The external accountants confirm they have everything.

rules.text: Never use an invoice with the wrong company name or tax ID; ask the supplier for a new one.
rules.why: A wrong invoice makes the return fail.

scenarios.situation: On the 9th you find one more purchase invoice from last month.
scenarios.question: What do you do?
options: Send it with this month's batch
Ask the external accountants which month to use
Leave it out
scenarios.explanation: The Pack has no answer yet for late invoices (OQ-002), so ask rather than guess.

processes.name: Count petty cash and close the safe
processes.summary: Every evening: count the petty cash, compare it with the book, attach the receipts, then lock the safe and both sign.

people.involvement: Present while the safe is open, and signs
Holds the safe combination, receives the closing form

steps.title: Close the door; two people present while the safe is open
steps.detail: Close the finance room door and keep a second person with you from opening to closing.
steps.why: No one outside sees the cash or the combination, and there is always a witness.

steps.title: Count the petty cash by note and coin
steps.detail: Count each denomination and write the counts on the cash count form.
steps.why: Counting by denomination makes mistakes easy to find.

steps.title: Compare with the petty cash book
steps.detail: The counted total must equal the balance in the petty cash book.
steps.why: A shortage or overage has to be known the same day, not at month end.
steps.check: The difference is $0. If not, follow R-004.

steps.title: Attach today's receipts to the vouchers
steps.detail: One receipt per voucher, stapled top left.
steps.why: They are needed to top up petty cash at month end.

steps.title: Lock the safe and spin the dial
steps.detail: Spin the dial several times after closing. The combination is not in this Pack; get it from the chief accountant.
steps.why: Stops anyone reopening it from the last position.

steps.title: Both sign the closing form
steps.detail: Sign, date and write the counted total, then put the form in the chief accountant's tray.
steps.why: It records who counted and what the total was.

rules.text: If the cash is short or over by any amount, record it on the form and tell the chief accountant the same day. Never add or remove money to make it match.
rules.why: Making it match hides the real problem.

scenarios.situation: The count is $4 short and it is almost 17:00.
scenarios.question: What do you do?
options: Put in $4 of your own
Record the shortage and tell the chief accountant today
Leave it and recount tomorrow
scenarios.explanation: R-004: any difference is recorded and reported the same day; never make it match yourself.

processes.name: Approve a supplier payment
processes.summary: Check the documents, confirm the supplier's bank account, and get the right person to approve by amount before the Friday payment run.
processes.trigger: An invoice arrives; payments go out every Friday

systems.name: Accounting system
systems.purpose: Record the bill and schedule the payment

steps.title: Check the documents are complete
steps.detail: There must be an invoice and an approved purchase order with the same amount and supplier name.
steps.why: Paying without a purchase order means paying for something the company did not order.
steps.branch_question: Is there an invoice and an approved purchase order?

steps.title: Check for a new supplier or changed bank account
steps.detail: Compare the bank account on the invoice with the supplier record in the accounting system.
steps.why: Fraudsters send fake emails asking to change bank details.
steps.branch_question: Is this a new supplier, or is the bank account different from the record?

steps.title: Call to confirm, using the number on the contract
steps.detail: Call the number in the contract or supplier record, never the one in the email. Note who confirmed and when.
steps.why: A number in a fake email leads to the fraudster.

steps.title: Check the amount to choose the approver
steps.detail: Use the invoice total including tax.
steps.why: Approval limits depend on the amount.

steps.title: Chief accountant approves; add to the Friday run
steps.detail: Send the documents to the chief accountant to sign, then schedule the payment in the accounting system.
steps.why: One run a week means fewer mistakes.

steps.title: General manager approves; add to the Friday run
steps.detail: Send it through the chief accountant to the general manager. If it is not signed by Thursday, move it to the next run.
steps.why: Large amounts need a director to see them.
steps.check: Signed by the general manager before it is scheduled.

steps.title: Return it with a list of what is missing
steps.detail: Reply to the requester and list the missing documents one by one.
steps.why: They can fix everything in one go.

rules.text: Every payment needs an invoice and an approved purchase order.
rules.why: Never pay for something the company did not order.

rules.text: For a new supplier or a changed bank account, confirm by calling the number on the contract, never the one in the email.
rules.why: Stops fake "change of bank details" emails.

rules.text: Over $5,000 needs the general manager's approval.
rules.why: The chief accountant can approve up to $5,000.

rules.text: Up to $200 can be paid from petty cash without waiting for the Friday run.
rules.why: Summarised from "small things we just pay in cash".
rules.source: AI summary of the interview; not confirmed yet

scenarios.situation: A regular supplier emails new bank details and a number to call back.
scenarios.question: How do you confirm?
options: Call the number in the email
Call the number on the contract or supplier record
Reply to the email and ask
scenarios.explanation: R-006: the email may be fake, and so may its phone number and reply address.

scenarios.situation: An invoice for $6,200 including tax, documents complete, existing supplier.
scenarios.question: Who approves it?
options: The chief accountant
The general manager
No one; schedule it
scenarios.explanation: R-007: over $5,000 needs the general manager.

processes.name: When online banking goes wrong
processes.summary: Common problems with online banking, their causes and what to do.
processes.trigger: Online banking does not work as usual

steps.title: Note the message and the time
steps.detail: A screenshot is fine, but cover account numbers and amounts before you pass it on.
steps.why: The bank and the chief accountant need the exact message.

troubleshooting.symptom: No one-time code arrives on the phone
troubleshooting.cause: The phone number on the user is still the previous officer's
troubleshooting.fix: Ask the chief accountant to have the bank change the number. Never ask for or use someone else's code.

troubleshooting.cause: The bank has not closed the day yet (before 10:00 on the 1st)
troubleshooting.fix: Wait until after 10:00 and download again.

troubleshooting.symptom: A transfer shows "pending" for more than an hour
troubleshooting.cause: It went to another bank after the cut-off time
troubleshooting.fix: Do not send it again. Check the next business morning; if it is still pending, call the bank helpline.

troubleshooting.symptom: Cannot log in: the account is locked
troubleshooting.fix: The chief accountant unlocks it on the admin page.

scenarios.situation: No code arrives. A colleague offers to receive it on their phone instead.
scenarios.question: What do you do?
options: Accept, to get the job done on time
Decline, and ask the chief accountant to change the number
Keep requesting a new code until one arrives
scenarios.explanation: T-002: a one-time code belongs to one person only. The real cause is the old phone number.

prerequisites: Online banking access for your own user
processes.escalation: Bank helpline first. If it is still not solved within a business day, or money may have gone to the wrong place, tell the chief accountant straight away.

processes.name: Track issued cheques
processes.summary: Follow every cheque from writing to clearing, chase the ones not banked, and void the ones that expire.
processes.trigger: A cheque is written; check the statement every Monday

systems.name: Cheque register (spreadsheet)
systems.purpose: One row per cheque and its status

steps.title: Record the cheque in the register
steps.detail: Cheque number, payee, amount and date, status "Written".
steps.why: Every open cheque explains part of a reconciliation difference.

steps.title: Get two signatures
steps.detail: Both authorised signers sign; set the status to "Signed".
steps.why: One signature is not valid for the company's bank.

steps.title: Hand it over and note the date
steps.detail: Give it to the payee against a signature, or post it; set the status to "Handed over".
steps.why: The 30-day and 6-month clocks start here.

steps.title: Check the statement every Monday
steps.detail: Look for the cheque number in online banking.
steps.why: Tells you which cheques have cleared.

steps.title: Remind the payee
steps.detail: Email the payee; set the status to "Overdue".
steps.why: Old cheques keep the reconciliation open.

steps.title: Void it; reissue only if still owed
steps.detail: Mark it "Expired", then "Voided" in the register. Ask the chief accountant before writing a new cheque.
steps.why: An expired cheque must never be paid twice.

steps.title: Mark it as cleared
steps.detail: Set the status to "Cleared" with the date it appeared on the statement.
steps.why: Closed cheques drop out of the reconciliation.

rules.text: Every cheque needs two authorised signatures.
rules.why: The bank rejects cheques with one signature.

rules.text: A cheque not presented within 6 months is void. Never write a replacement before voiding the first.
rules.why: Prevents paying the same bill twice.

scenarios.situation: A supplier says they lost a cheque you gave them 7 months ago and asks for a new one.
scenarios.question: What do you do first?
options: Write a new cheque straight away
Void the old one in the register, then ask the chief accountant about reissuing
Tell them it is too late
scenarios.explanation: R-010: void the first cheque before any replacement, so it can never be paid twice.
